messages:
maya: FYI — getting 3 separate support tickets (different tenants) reporting 429s right after last night's billing change. All show remaining quota in dashboard but API responses are being throttled. stack: hosted API -> rate-limiter v2 -> limiter-redis. can someone triage?

eli: Which tenants and sample req IDs? any correlation with specific models or regions?

maya: tenant ids: acme-inc, greenstack, monoai. sample x-request-id: 7c2f8a3b. headers they send include x-api-key + x-idempotency-key in some cases, others not.

dylan: quick glance at limiter logs for 7c2f8a3b:
```
[2026-03-17T02:12:03Z] limiter/decision request_id=7c2f8a3b tenant=acme-inc model=text-4x decision=DENY reason=burst_overlap bucket_tokens=0 reserved=1 window=60
[2026-03-17T02:12:03Z] limiter/cache hit key=burst:acme-inc:default fingerprint=fb9a2a reserved_by=worker-3
[2026-03-17T02:12:05Z] limiter/decision request_id=7c2f8a3b tenant=acme-inc decision=RELEASE reserved=1
```

maya: So limiter is denying even though dashboard shows tokens. Note the log shows reserved_by=worker-3 then RELEASE shortly after. customers see intermittent 429s.

eli: Was anything changed to burst/window config last night?

ana: I applied a config tweak at 23:45UTC: set enable_sticky_burst=true and burst_window_seconds=120 (was 60). It was intended to reduce churn when requests cluster.

dylan: That matches. I suspect a race in the sticky-reservations path: when enable_sticky_burst is true we write a reservation key keyed by fingerprint. If multiple workers compute the same fingerprint concurrently (idempotency-key missing or colliding), they can double-reserve then one releases and leaves bucket at 0 for a short time. Also fingerprint generation was changed to include model+tenant only in the last deploy, dropping per-request nonce.

support-ana: Customers are pushing for ETA — they're losing production traffic. Any hotfix?

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2189 assigned to dylan. Pager escalated to oncall.

eli: Repro steps I ran locally: send 10 parallel requests without idempotency-key for same tenant/model, with small token budget configured per-second. Observed multiple reservations and 4-5 DENY responses, despite aggregate quota showing available.

maya: Good repro. What's safest immediate mitigation? rollback config?

dylan: Proposed mitigations (in order):
1) Set enable_sticky_burst=false (instant config rollback) — should stop fingerprint-based reservations.
2) Run a small script to clear currently reserved burst keys in Redis to free stuck reservations: `redis-cli -h limiter-redis KEYS "burst:acme-inc:*" | xargs -r redis-cli -h limiter-redis DEL` (repeat per affected tenant).
3) Deploy a patch that reintroduces per-request nonce into the fingerprint and adds a compare-and-set when reserving to avoid double-counts (PR #4087).

ana: Rolling back enable_sticky_burst now. Pushing change to prod. ETA ~5m.

sre-bot: Config rollback completed. Change-id cfg-2026-0921.

eli: After rollback, I reran parallel repro against acme-inc: DENYs dropped from 40% -> 2% (likely valid transient edge cases).

support-ana: Support notified customers with interim mitigation: temporary config rollback and suggested clients add idempotency-key if possible. Offering one-day credit pending postmortem.

dylan: Next steps:
- I'll own the patch PR to fix fingerprinting and atomic reserve (target: merge and canary within 24h).
- Run a job to scan limiter-redis and remove stale reservations older than 30s; add TTL to reservations (short-term hotfix).
- Postmortem draft by me in 48h after full root cause verification.

maya: Thanks. Please add runbook updates: document risks of enable_sticky_burst, and add a canary for burst behavior in ci that sends parallel requests to detect regressions.

eli: Also add a dashboard alarm for reservation_count / reserve_release_ratio — we had reserve spikes but release pattern was noisy.

support-ana: Closing loop with customers this morning. Will reopen if any new 429s.

dylan: Patch PR #4087 linked in repo, will ping when ready for canary.

maya: Good job team. Recording this thread for the post-incident notes.
